titre_page: How to make a visual novel (choice story) without code? | Yop2D guide
description: Make a visual novel on an Android tablet or phone, with no code and nothing to import: a ready-made character, lines, choices, several endings, a title screen with saves, friendship hearts. A step-by-step guide with the [[dire_phrase]] and [[poser_choix]] nodes.
h1: How to make a choice story (visual novel)?
carte: A character who talks, a question, several endings, a title screen with “Continue” and friendship hearts.
etapes: {{poser_choix}}: each answer leaves by its own output towards a different story.
{{terminer_histoire}} with an ending name, and {{ecran_titre_histoire}} at the start: “Continue”, “New game”, “Endings and gallery”.
{{changer_amitie}} after a kind answer, {{tester_amitie}} to pick the ending.
blocs: A visual novel is an illustrated story where the player reads dialogues and makes choices that change what happens next. With Yop2D, everything is done with your finger, without writing a script, and **without importing anything**: the library already has a ready-made character (Hana, with several emotions) and watercolor backgrounds. You don't even need to place anything in the scene: the nodes show the background, the characters and the text box by themselves.
a new empty project (an empty scene is enough).

In Yop2D, the built-in guide **“My first story”** (home screen, guides card) does steps 1 and 2 with you in 5 minutes: a yellow frame shows where to tap, even inside windows. To see everything you can do, download the **Firefly Night** example in the Examples tab.
Video: a choice story made with Yop2D, without a single line of code.
Step 1: a background and a first line
Add **[[changer_decor]]** and pick an image, for example the meadow.
Add **[[dire_phrase]]**. Tap **{{lang:dire_phrase.personnage}}**, then **＋ New character…**, then **⭐ Ready-made character**, and pick **Hana**. Next time, Hana will be right in the list.
Tap **{{lang:dire_phrase.phrase}}** and write what she says, for example: “Hello! Did you just arrive here?”. You can also pick her **{{lang:dire_phrase.emotion}}**.
Link the three nodes in order, then play: the background appears, Hana comes in and talks, letter by letter.
Add **[[poser_choix]]** and link it after Hana's line.
Write **{{lang:poser_choix.reponse1}}**: “Yes!” and **{{lang:poser_choix.reponse2}}**: “No thanks”. You can have up to 4 answers.

The node has one output per answer. Link the [[lang:port_reponse1]] output to a new [[dire_phrase]] (happy Hana: “Great! Come, I'll show you the village.”), and the [[lang:port_reponse2]] output to another one (sad Hana: “Oh… too bad.”).
Play and try both answers: the story branches like a tree.

While playing, the player can tap **◀ Back** to go back to the previous line, even before a choice, to try the other answer. The History, Auto, Skip, saves and settings buttons fold into a single ☰ menu.
Step 3: endings and a title screen
At the end of each branch, add **[[terminer_histoire]]**. Give it an **ending name**, for example “The village tour” or “Alone on the road”.
Add **[[ecran_titre_histoire]]** right after **[[NoeudEventStart]]**, write your story's title, and link its [[lang:port_nouvelle_partie]] output to **[[changer_decor]]**.
Link each **[[terminer_histoire]]** to **[[ecran_titre_histoire]]**: after an ending, the player goes back to the title screen.

Play: the title screen offers “New game”, then “Continue” (the story saves itself at every line) and “Endings and gallery” (the endings found, with a souvenir picture, and the backgrounds already seen).
Step 4: friendship hearts that change the ending
After a kind answer, add **[[changer_amitie]]**: **{{lang:changer_amitie.personnage}}** Hana, **{{lang:changer_amitie.ajout}}** 1. Hearts appear at the top left and a “+1 ❤” floats up.
Before the ending, add **[[tester_amitie]]**: Hana, at least 2 hearts.
Link the [[lang:port_vrai]] output to the happy ending, and the [[lang:port_faux]] output to a sadder one. The hearts are kept in the save, and **◀ Back** puts them back as they were.
**[[montrer_personnage]]** brings a character in or out without talking; each character can have its place on screen (left, middle, right).
**[[demander_texte]]** asks the player's name: in the lines, `{prenom}` shows it.
**[[ambiance]]** adds rain, storm, snow, petals, fireflies or night, with their sounds; **[[transition_ecran]]** and **[[zoom_ecran]]** add rhythm.
In **{{lang:dire_phrase.personnage}}**, **🎨 Dialogue style…** changes the text box: character portrait in the box, ☰ menu, hearts shown or not, lines read aloud.

Each answer of [[poser_choix]] can have a picture (advanced settings): the answers become big illustrated cards. An answer can also require a condition, and a timer adds the [[lang:port_temps_ecoule]] output.
The **🗺** button of the {{lang:titre_blueprint}} opens the **story map**: all branches, choices and endings at a glance; tapping a box takes you to the right node.
Each line can be written in 9 languages: the game shows the player's language.
**Nothing shows up:** check that [[NoeudEventStart]] is linked to the first node, and that each node is linked to the next.
**The line shows without a character:** **{{lang:dire_phrase.personnage}}** is empty, or it's the narrator. Pick Hana in the list.
**“Continue” doesn't appear:** there is no saved game yet. Start a “New game” and read at least one line.
**An ending doesn't count in “Endings and gallery”:** give it an **ending name** in [[terminer_histoire]].
**The player is stuck after an ending:** link [[terminer_histoire]] to [[ecran_titre_histoire]], or to another scene.
